# 2017 STEAMWORKS – hindsight

Source: user hindsight notes, batch 1 (2026-09-27).

## Game play / meta
- Dominant concept: **a shooter with large ball capacity** (at least 50; elite robots closer to 100), fed directly
  from the hopper in AUTO, with an effective **wide ground intake** for balls in TELEOP – either two lanes or a turret –
  plus a **gear ground intake** (minimal width, reaching slightly outside the bumper through a hole to stay minimal).
- Double-shooter AUTOs were elite, but alliances rarely did double hoppers. Elite gear robots were also important:
  some alliances did 4 gear stages plus as much shooting as possible, others 2–3 stages with much more shooting time.
- **Everyone climbed.** The gear ground intake was on a pivot and also placed the gears on the peg.
- **Hidden score trick:** human players staged the level 3 and 4 gears only in the last few seconds of the match (even
  though robots placed those gears much earlier). The other alliance sometimes thought it had a big lead and did not
  change strategy, then the score jumped at once.

## Dominant robots
- **254 / 973** – two-lane shooters with huge capacity and a fast rate; small-package ground gear intake. Ball
  indexing: 254 an active roller floor, 973 a double spindexer.
- **118 / 1690** – turret shooter with active funneling using belts/polycord; the same kind of ground gear intake.
- **125 / 971** – turret shooter with huge capacity and a high rate; indexing by a dye rotor (paintball-inspired).
- **1011 / 148 (offseason)** – gear-only robot with a wide ground intake; since that was all they had on the robot,
  they were very light and geared for very high acceleration and speed. 148 took it to perfection in the offseason
  and did about 15 gears per match (more than needed), far more than other teams.

## Effective mechanisms
- **1011 / 1619 / 148 (offseason)** wide ground intake for gears; the same mechanism placed the gear. Top and bottom
  kicker rollers (bottom rollers of smaller diameter?).
- **1690 / 254** small-footprint ground gear intake; the same mechanism placed the gear. Top and bottom kicker rollers
  (bottom rollers of smaller diameter?).
- **118** active funneling using polycord.
- **254 active roller floor** – a set of round tubes indexing balls quickly into the shooter.
- **254 ground intake** – super effective "touch it, own it", acquiring a mass of balls at once.
- **254 / 973 double shooter** – two lanes (in 2026 teams improved this into wider shooters without dividers).
- **1986** – single spindexer, shooting only from adjacent to the goal.
- **973 double spindexer** – not the best spindexer (2026 had better ones), but the idea started here.
- **118 / 254 / 1577 velcro climb** (everyone did it) – velcro on a rotating round tube; the rope attaches and acts
  as a winch to lift the robot.
- **1574 offline-adjustable shooter** – they wanted mechanically aligned AUTO shots from the wall of the hopper, but
  the needed angle was not easy to reach; so they fixed the shooter angle and could switch it offline between two
  modes for the red and blue alliance (required by the field symmetry).
- **2122** – the 118 / 1690 concept but without a ground ball intake, to simplify a bit (balls only from the hopper,
  during AUTO). Not elite level, but world level.
  - **2767** under-the-bumper gear intake.
